title: Rook captures and blocked paths
objectives: Recognize that a rook stops at the first piece in its path

steps.text: A rook can't jump over pieces. If a friendly piece is in the way, the rook must stop before it. If an enemy piece is in the way, the rook can capture it — but then it must stop there.

steps.prompt: Find the rook's one legal move — it's blocked in one direction and can capture in the other.

feedback.default: The rook is blocked by its own pawn on c4 in one direction, and can only reach d4 by capturing the black rook there.

steps.successExplanation: Rxd4 is the only legal move — the pawn on c4 blocks the other direction, so capturing the rook on d4 is forced.

steps.prompt: A rook can jump over a piece if it really needs to reach the other side.

feedback.default: The rook can never jump over any piece, friendly or enemy.

steps.successExplanation: Right — a blocked rook has to stop or capture right there. It never has the option to jump.

steps.prompt: Capture the bishop with your rook.

feedback.default: Look for the rook's one enemy target along its rank — the path there needs to be clear, and the rook can't cross its own pawn on c4 to reach anything the other way.

steps.successExplanation: Rxg4 captures the bishop. The path along the 4th rank to g4 was completely clear, so the rook could slide the whole way and capture.

steps.summary: You've mastered the rook: it moves and captures in straight lines, any distance, but stops dead at the first piece — friend or foe — in its path.
